subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed for existing ownerless session rows, or should OpenClaw provide a supported migration/ownership-adoption path before enforcing the new `sessions.patch` fence?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but legacy ownerless rows have no authenticated plugin authority; choosing rejection versus migration changes upgrade behavior and cannot be resolved safely from code review alone.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownerless rows
options.body: Merge the current behavior, retaining non-plugin operator access and documenting that legacy ownerless rows cannot be patched by plugin-runtime callers.

options.title: Add a migration path first
options.body: Define a narrow doctor or owner-controlled migration that assigns ownership before the runtime fence applies to legacy rows.

options.title: Keep current legacy behavior temporarily
options.body: Preserve ownerless plugin patching until a shared ownership policy covers both patch and create paths.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Merge the current behavior, retaining non-plugin operator access and documenting that legacy ownerless rows cannot be patched by plugin-runtime callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion identifies a maintainer-level compatibility choice and directly requests their review.
